column1: # Floently — Card hint authoring sample
# This CSV is a representative authoring pass to set the format and Finnish
# style for hints across the card bank. Twelve hints across three content
# types × three CEFR bands. Each hint:
#   1. Is in Finnish (the hint is part of the Finnish-immersion experience)
#   2. Points at the structure of the answer
#   3. Is short (1 line) — long hints become explanations
#   4. Uses level-appropriate vocabulary (A1 hints don't use C1 metalanguage)
# Format:
#   card_id        — matches the card's id field
column2: OR a wildcard for a class

column1: #                    of cards (e.g. "vocabulary:healthcare:A1-A2:*")
#   content_type   — vocabulary_card | sentence_card | grammar_card
#   level_band     — A1-A2 | B1-B2 | C1-C2
#   topic          — semantic field (vocabulary) or grammar focus
#   hint_fi        — the authored Finnish hint
#   notes_for_reviewer — what I'm trying to do; the reviewer can tighten
# REVIEW EXPECTED. I'm reasonably confident in the Finnish here
# native or near-native speaker should pass over this before it ships
# especially the C1-C2 hints where idiomatic register matters more.
# Specific concerns I'd flag for review:
#   - Use of "tarkista" vs "mieti" vs "muista" — all valid
#   - Whether hints reading like teacher-talk feel right or condescending
#   - Whether C1-C2 hints are pitched at the right level of metalanguage
# To use:
#   1. Reviewer revises hint_fi column and notes_for_reviewer
#   2. Bulk-load: hints get written to card.hint via a migration script
#      (not included — straightforward jq-style merge by card_id)
#   3. The backend resolver in cards_logic.py automatically picks up
#      authored hints over the synthesized fallback
card_id
# At A1-A2 we point at the most concrete possible context. The student is
# building a mental link between sound and meaning; a contextual cue ("at
# the doctor's"
vocab:basic:greetings:A1:hello
column5: Tämä sana on yleisin tapa tervehtiä Suomessa.
column6: Pointing at usage frequency rather than meaning. Could also say 'käytetään päivittäin'.

column1: vocab:healthcare:A1:medicine
column6: Semantic field cue. Does not give meaning directly.

column1: vocab:work:A1:colleague
column6: Slightly more revealing than I'd like — could tighten to 'liittyy työpaikkaan' if too obvious.

column1: vocab:nursing:B1:medication_round
column5: Tämä sana kuvaa toistuvaa hoitotehtävää osastolla.
column6: Healthcare-specific framing. Tests whether 'lääkkeenjako' or similar comes to mind via context.

column1: vocab:medical:C1:differential_diagnosis
column5: Tämä on diagnostinen prosessi jossa erotellaan vaihtoehtoisia syitä oireille.
column6: More technical framing. C1-C2 students can handle metalanguage; the hint frames the concept rather than the word.

column1: # Sentence hints point at the grammatical operation the student must perform.
# At A1-A2 we name basic categories ("the verb is in past tense"). At B1-B2
# we ask the student to make the call themselves. At C1-C2 we hint at register
# or pragmatic choices.
sent:partitive:A2:water
column5: Verbin objekti on jakaantuvaa ainetta — mikä sijapääte siihen tulee?
column6: Specific to drinks/food (partitive of substance). 'Jakaantuvaa ainetta' is the canonical school explanation.

column1: sent:locative:A2:home
column5: Mietitkö, oletko jossakin (inessiivi) vai menetkö jonnekin (illatiivi)?
column6: Tests whether student picks the right locative case. Direct, not too easy.

column1: sent:conditional:B1:would_help
column5: Tämä on epäsuora pyyntö tai ehto — minkä modaalisen muodon tarvitset?
column6: Testing -isi- ending recognition. Pragmatic framing (request vs condition).

column1: sent:passive:B2:building_built
column5: Lauseessa ei ole tekijää — mikä rakenne sopii kun tekijää ei mainita?
column6: Passive voice cue. Common B1-B2 stumbling block; this hint is one of the more 'teacher-talk' ones.

column1: sent:participial:C1:academic
column5: Tämä on tiivistetty rakenne joka korvaa että-lauseen — mietitkö aktiivin vai passiivin partisiippia?
column6: C1-C2 register-aware. 'Tiivistetty rakenne' is academic Finnish framing.

column1: # Grammar hints reference the rule abstractly enough that the student must
# apply it
column2: not just recall the answer. We avoid stating the rule outright

column1: # unless the rule has multiple branches the student must pick between.
gram:vowel_harmony:A1
column5: Sanan vokaalit kuuluvat samaan ryhmään (etu- tai takavokaaleihin) — kumpaan tämän sanan vokaalit kuuluvat?
column6: Vowel harmony is the canonical A1-A2 rule. Hint forces categorization without giving answer.

column1: gram:consonant_gradation:B1:strong_weak
column5: Konsonantti vaihtuu kun tavu muuttuu avoimeksi tai suljetuksi — mikä vaihtelutyyppi tähän pätee (kk/k vai pp/p)?
column6: Consonant gradation is THE B1-B2 morphology challenge. Hint names the operation and asks the student to identify the type.
